chunks: From him, from Abī Jaʿfar, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the muleteers who hire out riding animals, traveling about every few days; whenever some work comes to them, they go out. So he said: shortening is upon them when they travel.

key_terms.الدَّوَابَّ: beasts of transport or riding animals
key_terms.الْمُكَارِينَ: muleteers or those who hire out animals for transport
key_terms.يَخْتَلِفُونَ: they go back and forth or travel repeatedly
key_terms.يُكْرُونَ: they rent out or hire out for use

ai.seo_question: Do muleteers and transport workers shorten their salat (prayer) while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning muleteers and those who regularly hire out animals for transport. It states that when they travel, they are subject to qasr, meaning they perform shortened prayer in travel despite the recurring nature of their journeys.
